claim: Within one generated changing prediction family, independently scored consequences of prior inheritance choices cause an actor-authored, controller-committed selection policy to improve later held-out behavior, become harmful, be corrected by later contact, and retain capacity for another correction.
target_scope: Private, time-bounded, single-family OT-1 evidence only; no OT-2, OT-3, cross-domain, immutable-weight, or public-reconstruction claim.
seed_exclusions: no useful selection criterion or operation is named, enumerated, exemplified, or encoded as a mode switch
no regime identity, order, transition, answer, or expected correction is actor-visible

the words and concepts abstraction, exception preservation, recency weighting, drift response, noise rejection, corroboration threshold, and confidence weighting are absent from selector-facing seed and developer instructions

candidate.policy_representation: bounded free-form text; no researcher-authored strategy menu

stage_causal_order: apply the current committed policy to the stage contact archive and unlabeled contact queries in a fresh selector encounter
give only those selected contacts and queries to a fresh predictor and retain the independent contact outcome as a protected receipt unavailable to heldout branches
evaluate the current committed policy, its protected parent, and fixed controls on the same heldout archive and queries in the frozen counterbalanced order
seal every heldout branch, then give only the protected contact receipt and current policy to a fresh selector-update encounter
commit every exact-schema-valid bounded proposal as the next stage's policy without consulting heldout outcomes; the final post-canary proposal is retained but not scored

rubric: identify a concrete inclusion, exclusion, weighting, comparison, consolidation, or update operation instantiated by the proposal
confirm the operation is not semantically present in the seed orientation or offered as a researcher-authored option
confirm selection receipts show the operation changed selected event identities
confirm deterministic changed-versus-frozen scores show material held-out benefit
reject new labels, paraphrases, self-reports, or unused policy prose
novelty_review.authority_limit: Reviewers judge seed novelty only and cannot alter world outcomes, deterministic scores, commits, or final causal gates.

required_receipts: seed orientation and initial policy identities
protected raw archive and rejected-event sample identities
every selector proposal and controller accept or deny decision
matched changed and frozen policy selection identities
fresh predictor actions and independent world outcomes
selector-change ablation and protected predecessor branch
later harm, corrective revision, recovery, and post-correction capacity canary
blinded novelty rubric identities and decisions
fresh context, direct tool inventory, hosted model epoch, task order, budget, audit, and reproduction identities
promotion_gate: all hypothesis, seed, policy/projection budgets, task generation, regime order, task order, controls, branch semantics, score thresholds, novelty rubric, models, receipt parser, evaluator, implementation, and private task identities are frozen before candidate outputs
at least two non-correction revisions causally beat their frozen predecessors in both workers
at least one materially used operation absent from the seed passes both blinded reviews in both workers
a learned policy is later harmful relative to its protected predecessor in both workers
later contact causes a committed correction that passes recovery and selector-change ablation gates in both workers
the post-correction canary passes in both workers
the changed lineage passes absolute and fixed-control comparative gates in both workers
all freshness, authority, leak, parse, tool, resource, deployment-epoch, audit, evidence, and clean-reproduction gates pass
red_line_review: The seed supplies capability and authority but no useful selection strategy or strategy menu.
Policy prose has no evidentiary value without changed selection identities and deterministic downstream benefit.
The actor may propose but cannot commit selector state or alter archive, outcomes, branches, reviews, or scores.
Protected rejected-event sampling prevents the selector from choosing all evidence used to judge itself.
Changed and frozen branches use identical event pools, queries, predictor model, prompts, budgets, and task order.
Within each stage the current-policy contact probe and every heldout branch seal before a proposal commits for the next stage; no update sees heldout outcomes.
The controller rejects duplicate, unknown, or non-budgeted selected event identities; the hosted response-schema dialect is not trusted to enforce uniqueness.
Every selector, predictor, and reviewer encounter uses a fresh thread and workspace.
No local model inference is used.
